Noumbiel : lancement des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV) à Batié
items.description: BURKINA-ELIMINATION-GITE-LARVAIRE-NOUMBIEL Noumbiel : lancement des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV) à Batié Batié, 05 septembre (2026) – Dans le cadre des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle, la province du Noumbiel a mobilisé, samedi à Batié, une synergie d'action sur le terrain, afin de détruire les gîtes larvaires mais aussi sensibiliser les populations à leur élimination afin de lutter efficacement contre le paludisme et ses corollaires. L’objectif est de réduire la transmission du paludisme et d'autres maladies vectorielles, à travers la destruction des gîtes larvaires mais aussi l'assainissement du cadre de vie. Du premier responsable de la province au citoyen lambda, le communiqué officiel du Président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Batié, Issoufou Sory a été bien entendu. Le Médecin chef du district sanitaire de Batié, Roland Wendnonga Konkobo, a invité les populations à supprimer les eaux stagnantes, les dépôts d'ordures et les herbes haute. Il a aussi recommandé aux habitants de retirer de leurs cadres de vie et de travail les récipients abandonnés pouvant contenir de l'eau. Pour l'occasion, le haut-commissaire de la province, Drissa Hema a salué et remercié les participants pour la mobilisation. Il a exhorté l'ensemble des populations à continuer dans le même élan afin de lutter contre le paludisme conformément à la vision des plus hautes autorités : « zéro paludisme » à l'horizon 2030. Agence d'information du Burkina HO/ata/zs

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El PP carga contra el Gobierno tras los informes sobre Ceuta: “Había avisos y no hicieron nada”
items.description: El PP ha salido en tromba contra el Gobierno tras la publicación esta tarde de los documentos desclasificados sobre la crisis de Ceuta, emitidos entre el 1 de julio y el 1 de agosto por diversos organismos, como el CNI, la inteligencia militar, la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil. En redes sociales, figuras como Miguel Tellado o Ester Muñoz han denunciado que los documentos prueban que “sí había avisos” y que el Gobierno mintió y “no hizo nada”. “El problema no es el CNI, como ha dicho hoy Sánchez. El problema es él”, ha escrito Muñoz. “Sánchez miente, lo sabían y no hicieron nada”, ha publicado la cuenta oficial del PP. El partido hace hincapié en uno de los documentos, del día 29, en el que el CNI alertó a los servicios de inteligencia de Marruecos de “convocatorias” por Whatsapp con nombres como “Asalto a la valla de Ceuta” y grupos de Facebook. Otros documentos hablan de la “pasividad” de Marruecos una vez comenzada la avalancha. Por otro lado, la Comisión Europea ha concedido a España 114,7 millones de euros para reforzar la vigilancia y protección fronteriza y financiar infraestructuras y tecnología de seguridad, incluidos equipos de cámaras térmicas y sistemas de observación, barreras flotantes y drones submarinos. items.title: Yoto : Des kits scolaires aux élèves de l’EPP Kouvé Atran
items.description: Tabligbo, 9 sept. (ATOP) – Les élèves de l’École primaire publique (EPP) Kouvé Atran, dans la commune Yoto 1, ont bénéficié de kits scolaires, le mardi 8 septembre dans les locaux de l’établissement. Au total, 254 élèves, dont 126 filles, issus des classes du CP1 au CM2 au titre de l’année scolaire 2025-2026, ont reçu chacun un kit composé de cahiers, d’ensembles géométriques, de stylos, d’ardoises, de crayons, de gommes et de crayons de couleur. Le don a été financé par un natif de la localité, Dr Akakpo Rodolphe, résidant à Paris, à travers l’Association pour le bien-être humain (ABEH). Ce geste de solidarité vise à promouvoir l’excellence en milieu scolaire en apportant un soutien aux apprenants afin de leur permettre d’entamer la nouvelle année scolaire dans de bonnes conditions. À travers cette initiative, le donateur réaffirme son attachement à son village natal et son engagement à accompagner les efforts visant à offrir aux enfants de Kouvé de meilleures conditions pour apprendre et réussir. Le représentant du donateur, M. Agbo Yaogan, a félicité le bienfaiteur pour son engagement constant en faveur des élèves, de l’établissement et de la communauté. Il a souhaité que ce geste contribue à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage des bénéficiaires et a encouragé d’autres bonnes volontés à emboîter le pas au donateur. Le porte-parole des enseignants, Kapa Tassimlia, a salué cet accompagnement qui constitue une source de motivation pour les apprenants et les encourage à redoubler d’efforts. Il a rassuré que les bénéficiaires feront bon usage des dons afin de travailler dans de meilleures conditions et d’obtenir de bons résultats au terme de l’année scolaire. Le président de l’association des parents d’élèves de l’EPP Kouvé Atran, Kradi Yawo, le président du comité de gestion des écoles primaires, Guébé Komi Moïse, ainsi que des enseignants et des parents d’élèves ont pris part à cette cérémonie. ATOP/SAK/AJA

items.title: Adutwum proposes subject resits, transcript system for secondary schools
items.description: Former Education Minister and Member of Parliament for Bosomtwe, Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum, has called for reforms to Ghana’s education system to allow students who fail individual subjects to resit them or, where necessary, repeat a class. Speaking on The Pulse on JoyNews on Wednesday, September 9, Dr Adutwum believes such measures could help address the large number of students who struggle to meet the requirements for progression to tertiary education because of poor grades in key subjects. Under the system, students’ academic performance would be recorded throughout their time in school rather than relying mainly on their final examination results. “What it means is that every semester when students take their final exams, it’s reported to a portal maintained by WAEC,” he explained. He said the system would give the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) access to students’ academic records and provide a clearer picture of their performance over time. Dr Adutwum said a properly implemented transcript system should also be linked to opportunities for students to resit subjects they fail, similar to the system used at university level. “At the university, if you fail a class, what happens to you? You do a resit,” he said. He questioned why a similar opportunity should not be available to secondary school students who fail individual subjects. “So if you are doing Form One English and you have an F in your own assessment by your own teacher, why do you move to second semester and get another F? Nothing is said to you, nobody asks you for a resit, then you go to Form Two, you have F9 first semester, no need for resit,” he said. He said that students could otherwise continue accumulating poor grades in a particular subject until they reach their final year without receiving adequate intervention. “There should be an opportunity for the student to be helped to resit those courses,” Dr Adutwum said. He believes the transcript system would make such interventions easier by identifying students who are struggling early enough. “Because all the students who got a D7 to F9, we should have known that they were going to get it,” he said. When asked whether students who fail should be allowed to repeat a class, Dr Adutwum said that should be an option where a student has failed a significant number of subjects. “If you fail a certain number of courses,” he said. He explained that schools already have the authority to repeat students where it is considered necessary, although the process should involve parents or guardians. He said parents should not be surprised by a decision that their child is being made to repeat a class. “There is also a requirement that the parents should be informed; they should be in the loop,” he said. According to Dr Adutwum, schools should first engage parents and discuss the student’s academic difficulties before deciding on repetition. He proposed a process where the school meets the parents, identifies the student’s weaknesses and puts interventions in place. “Come, let’s discuss this, call a parent conference, where you sit down and say your child Kojo Mensah is not doing well. We are going to prescribe some intervention for him; we are going to give him extra work to do to make up this grade,” he said. If those interventions fail, he said, repeating the class should remain an option. “If it doesn’t work out, Kojo Mensah will be repeated,” he said. Dr Adutwum maintained that there is nothing preventing schools from repeating students where necessary, provided the decision is taken in the best interest of the child. “And the school has the right to repeat. There’s nothing that says a school cannot repeat a child,” he said. “Because it’s in the interest of the child when, for one reason or the other, they are not doing well,” he added. Dr Adutwum said a more comprehensive transcript and resit system could also help prevent situations where students are blocked from progressing to university because of a single poor grade. items.title: Yatenga/Namissiguima : des communautés mobilisées pour une opération volontaire de collecte de sang
items.description: Yatenga/Namissiguima : des communautés mobilisées pour une opération volontaire de collecte de sang Namissiguima, 9 sept. 2026 (AIB)- Après le succès de l'opération de collecte de sang la semaine dernière, les CSPS de Namissiguima et de Ramatoulaye, avec l'appui de la Croix rouge et du Centre national de transfusion sanguine (CNTS), antenne de Ouahigouya, ont organisé une troisième sortie dans la commune où 126 poches de sang ont été collectées, a constaté l’AIB sur place. Cette collecte de sang a été organisée dans le souci de combler le déficit en produits sanguins dans la région de Yaadga. Le Centre national de transfusion sanguine (CNTS), antenne de Ouahigouya a appuyé techniquement cette collecte volontaire de sang à Ramatoulaye, portant à trois, leur sortie dans la commune. Ainsi, 40 poches ont été prélevées à Namissiguima, 46 à Kononga et 40 à Ramatoulaye, soit 126 poches au total au cours de l'opération. Pour le point focal du don de sang de la Croix rouge, le camarade Boukary Ouédraogo, son organisation s'est portée volontaire pour accompagner le CNTS dans la collecte de sang dans la province du Yatenga. « C'est une activité régalienne de notre structure surtout que la demande est forte en cette période. Nous sommes satisfaits des différentes sorties dans la commune de Namissiguima et nous invitons les autres communes à se mobiliser pour cette activité citoyenne pour sauver des vies », a soutenu le camarade Ouédraogo. Un des nombreux donneurs du précieux liquide, Abdoul Bachid Maïga, dit trouver le courage et la volonté de donner son sang tout simplement parce que le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a donné l'exemple en donnant son sang, et a exhorté les populations qui le peuvent de marcher dans ses pas pour sauver des vies. Agence d'Information du Burkina. AZ/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: NUPRC threatens sanctions over unutilised gas flare sites
items.description: Warns firms of possible award revocation By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja ABUJA — The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NUPRC, has threatened to sanction companies awarded flare gas sites under the Nigerian Gas Flare Commercialisation Programme, NGFCP, if they fail to make significant progress towards developing and utilising the sites. The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this in Abuja during a working visit to the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo. A statement by the Commission’s Head of Corporate Communications and Media, Eniola Akinkuotu, said Eyesan presented an update on the implementation of the NGFCP during the visit. She explained that the Commission evaluates the performance of awardees one year after an award is granted to determine whether sufficient progress has been made towards developing and utilising the flare gas sites. “One year after an award has been granted, the Commission conducts an evaluation to determine whether there has been considerable progress,” Eyesan said. “Where there is insufficient progress, the Commission will take appropriate regulatory action, including revocation of the award where necessary,” she added. Eyesan said the NGFCP had continued to record progress despite initial resistance from some operators. According to her, 43 flare gas sites were initially identified for award under the programme, with 27 sites successfully awarded and implementation efforts ongoing. The NGFCP is aimed at commercialising gas currently being flared by oil and gas operators, reducing routine gas flaring and creating economic value from the country’s gas resources. Eyesan said Nigeria currently had more than 215 trillion cubic feet, TCF, of proven natural gas reserves, with an estimated total reserve base of about 600 TCF. She said the country’s abundant gas resources provided a strong foundation for power generation, industrialisation, exports and broader economic development. The NUPRC boss also highlighted progress in implementing the Host Community Development Trust framework established under the Petroleum Industry Act, PIA. She said the framework was designed to address longstanding concerns in oil-producing communities and ensure that petroleum resources contributed to sustainable development. According to Eyesan, available data showed that the implementation of the trusts had contributed to reductions in oil theft and oil spills, while improving relationships between oil and gas operators and host communities. “To date, 173 Host Community Development Trusts have been incorporated, 147 have been funded, over 1,001 projects are currently ongoing, while more than 200 projects have been successfully commissioned across host communities,” she said. In his remarks, Ekpo called for deliberate and aggressive implementation of the country’s gas commercialisation programme to enable Nigeria meet its 2030 target of ending routine gas flaring. The minister said the country could no longer afford to waste its gas resources through flaring, urging stakeholders to convert the resources into products and services capable of driving economic development. “The core objective is to add value to our gas resources by converting them into critical products and services. We must move away from environmental pollution and toward productive resource utilisation,” Ekpo said. items.title: Les cadres de la Binah assistent 1000 élèves vulnérables de la préfecture
items.description: Pagouda, 9 sept. (ATOP) – Mille élèves vulnérables du jardin d’enfants jusqu’au lycée des neufs cantons de la préfecture de la Binah ont bénéficié des kits scolaires, le mardi 8 septembre à Pagouda. Les cadres de la Binah, à travers cette action de solidarité, ont également récompensé les meilleurs lauréats au BAC II 2026 par 20 ordinateurs portatifs. Ils ont offert du matériel didactique et des tables bancs aux différents établissements du milieu. L’honorable Gani remettant un PC à une élève Chaque kit scolaire est composé de deux paquets de 100 et 200 pages, d’un ensemble géométrique, des stylos et un paquet de crayons de couleurs ainsi que des kits coloriage pour les jardins d’enfants. Les 20 ordinateurs ont été répartis en deux pour les deux communes et 200 tables bancs aux établissements des neuf cantons de la préfecture. Le député Gani Koffi a fait savoir que cette initiative entend appuyer les efforts du Président du Conseil en matière d’éducation pour tous. Ce geste, a-t-il souligné, vient améliorer les conditions de travail des élèves pour une éducation de qualité et permettre aux apprenants d’aborder avec sérénité la nouvelle année scolaire. Le porte-parole des bénéficiaires, l’élève Yom Essosolim, a témoigné sa reconnaissance aux bienfaiteurs en leur promettant de meilleurs résultats en fin d’année scolaire afin de gagner davantage leur confiance. La cérémonie a connu la présence des députés, Ayim Patatèng, le préfet de la Binah, Ataba Abalounorou et du représentant du directeur régional de l’éducation de la Kara, M. Houndjafo Koffi. Des autorités locales, des chefs établissements, des forces de l’ordre et de sécurité, ainsi que des parents et autres acteurs du système éducatif du milieu ont assisté à l’événement. items.title: Filth: Sanwo-Olu declares state of emergency on waste management
items.description: To deploy 160 new compactor trucks, five transfer stations by Q2 2027 By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has declared a “state of emergency” on waste management in the state, citing mounting pressure on waste collection and the growing menace of indiscriminate dumping across the metropolis. The governor, however, unveiled short-, medium- and long-term measures aimed at clearing the current backlog of waste and improving the state’s waste management system. Sanwo-Olu, who spoke on Wednesday during an inspection tour of the Olusosun dump site in Ojota, Lagos, said the intervention became necessary following weeks of slow waste turnaround and what he described as uncoordinated advocacy. The governor was accompanied by his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab; and other senior government officials. “What we are seeing at Olusosun is a typical sight of the challenge. We are here to see what the problem is and to clearly declare a small state of emergency so that we can get out of this very unpleasant situation,” Sanwo-Olu said. He disclosed that the state government, in partnership with development partner Zoomlion, was constructing two new 2,400-metric-tonne Transfer Loading Stations at Olusosun and Solu 3 in Alimosho Local Government Area. According to him, the facilities would receive compacted waste before transferring it to two Material Recovery Sites under construction at Oke Osho in Epe and Erikitte in Badagry. “Each transfer station is designed to handle about 500 trucks per day. With the transfer loading stations, waste will be compacted and eventually taken to a material recovery site where it will be further sorted and broken into other uses,” he said. Sanwo-Olu projected that physical development on the facilities would become visible by the end of the year, while full operations were expected between the first and second quarters of 2027. For immediate relief, he said the state planned to increase the capacity of the Olusosun facility from between 250 and 350 trucks daily to between 350 and 450 trucks by increasing the number of tipping points from two or three to four or five. He added that road stabilisation work was underway at Solu 3, with grading expected to be completed within two to three weeks to allow continued waste reception. Similar stabilisation work, he said, was planned for Iwulepe in Ikorodu and Oke Osho in Epe. “We are hoping that before the end of next month, or in another six weeks, we will have four active dump sites: Olusosun, Solu 3, Iwulepe, and Oke Osho in Epe. And also a fifth one in Badagry, Erikitte,” the governor said. He explained that the additional disposal points would help reduce truck turnaround time, which could currently take as long as 12 hours, to only a few hours by providing closer disposal options. 160 new compactors coming On waste collection, Sanwo-Olu disclosed that the state government had ordered 160 new compactor trucks, with shipment expected to commence soon. “Landfill compactors for on-site compaction are also being procured,” he added. The governor said Zoomlion and Private Sector Participants, PSPs, would also procure additional trucks, while the state government would work with the operators to develop financing models that would enable them to expand their operations sustainably. The Chairman of the PSP Association, who joined the inspection tour, also agreed to a membership audit aimed at identifying inactive operators. The state government said although about 800 PSPs were registered, only an estimated 400 were effectively operating. “We don’t want to have 800 PSPs when it is actually only 400 that are effective,” an official said, adding that the exercise would create room for new investors. Sanwo-Olu also appealed to residents and tenement occupiers to pay for waste collection services. “Lagosians in particular, we just want service. We don’t want to pay for this service. I think this era has to stop. It’s so unfair to see people rendering service and people are not paying them,” he said. He said the monthly sanitation exercise, launched four months ago, as well as ongoing advocacy campaigns, would be better coordinated. According to the governor, the combination of new equipment, additional disposal sites, transfer stations and reforms in the PSP system was designed to address the state’s waste generation, disposal and conversion challenges in the long term. Indiscriminate dumping Sanwo-Olu also warned residents against indiscriminate disposal of refuse, announcing tougher enforcement measures against offenders. He said environmental officers would monitor both PSP operators and residents, adding that offenders could face prosecution before mobile and public courts. The governor said residents could not justify dumping refuse on roads, highways or drainage channels simply because a PSP operator failed to arrive at their homes within 24 hours. He also disclosed plans to restructure and reinforce the operations of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, with a view to deploying more personnel to field operations. “Waste is outside on the street; it’s not in their offices,” Sanwo-Olu said, insisting that the agency must become more operationally responsive. The governor acknowledged the government’s responsibility for addressing the current challenges but noted that Lagos’ rapid population growth was putting increasing pressure on existing waste management infrastructure. He said the volume of waste generated in the state continued to rise with its population, stressing that government, residents and waste operators all had roles to play in tackling the problem. Sanwo-Olu assured residents that the government would continue to monitor the situation and implement measures aimed at restoring a cleaner and more efficient waste management system across Lagos. items.title: Carrick confident Man Utd can go far in ‘magical’ Champions League
items.description: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United are strong enough to compete with Europe’s best on their return to the Champions League for the first time in three years. Carrick earned his position as permanent United boss after leading the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League in his interim spell last season. Having secured a place in Europe’s elite club competition, United kick off their league phase campaign on Thursday when they face Azerbaijani champions Sabah at Old Trafford. “It’s a magical competition. It’s where we all want to be. When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it,” Carrick told reporters on Wednesday. “I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years. It’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best. “We’re delighted to be here, but we’re not here to just enjoy the occasion. We’re here to do business and go as far as we possibly can.” In two of their last three appearances in the Champions League, the three-time European champions have crashed out at the group stage and have not progressed beyond the last 16 since 2019. United have also made a slow start to the Premier League season, taking just four points from fixtures against Hull, Ipswich and Everton. However, many of their better performances under Carrick have come against stronger opposition. United beat Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea in the second half of last season. “I think we’re capable of doing some really good things in this competition and going further down the line in this competition,” Carrick said. “Certainly not getting ahead of ourselves because some part of it is a new experience for some of the players. “But the boys are used to playing European football for the most part in different competitions and we’ll take that forward and we’ve got a squad that’s strong enough to compete.” In contrast to the record-setting spending by many of their Premier League rivals, United were only able to strengthen their midfield in the transfer window. United benefited last season from only playing 40 games — their lowest total since the 1914/15 campaign. Carrick, though, said his players had to embrace the challenge of a heavier workload. “We play Thursday, Sunday, Wednesday and it’s what we’re here for. It’s about managing the group and having trust in everyone able to play,” he said. Benjamin Sesko is in contention for his first start of the season after coming off the bench to score in Sunday’s 2-2 draw at Everton. Carrick confirmed Matthijs de Ligt is also nearing a comeback after nearly a year out with a back injury. AFP The post Carrick confident Man Utd can go far in ‘magical’ Champions League appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Yatenga/Séguénéga : la délégation spéciale tient sa première session extraordinaire après 10 mois de trêve
items.description: Yatenga/Séguénéga : la délégation spéciale tient sa première session extraordinaire après 10 mois de trêve Séguénéga, 9 sept. 2026 (AIB)– La Délégation spéciale de la commune de Séguénéga a tenu le mardi 8 septembre 2026 sa première session extraordinaire où elle a délibéré sur plusieurs dossiers et adopté à l'unanimité, le budget rectificatif qui s'élève à 201 480 516 FCFA, a constaté l’AIB sur place. La présente session a été présidée par le camarade Yacouba Guiro, Président de la Délégation spéciale par intérim de la commune de Séguénéga. Plusieurs points ont été inscrits à l'ordre du jour de cette session extraordinaire entre autres, l'examen et adoption du premier budget rectificatif 2026. Le PDS par intérim, Yacouba Guiro a remercié les autorités pour la confiance placée en lui. «Ça fait longtemps que la commune n’a pas eu l’occasion d’organiser une session. Mais comme l’administration est une continuité, nous demandons à Dieu de nous accompagner. Notre souhait est d’avoir un cadre d’échanges fructueux qui contribuera à la bonne marche de notre commune », a-t-il déclaré. Le rapport de l’ordonnateur sur le 1er budget rectificatif 2026 a noté la suspension des interventions de plusieurs partenaires techniques et financiers. Au cours des travaux, la rapporteure de la Commission affaires économiques et financières, Mariam Barry a mis en avant la mobilisation des ressources à travers la vente aux enchères d’animaux mis en fourrière et l’attribution de boutiques aux commerçants. Un projet de délibération portant révision des taxes sur l’enlèvement des agrégats a été adopté. Il fixe à 5 000 FCFA pour le sable, moellons et gravillons pour les bennes de moins de 10 roues et 8 000 FCFA pour celles de 10 roues et plus. Pour les minerais, 7 000 FCFA et 10 000 FCFA respectivement. Les petits tricycles paieront 500 FCFA et les gros 1 000 FCFA. Un budget rectificatif de 201 480 516 FCFA a été adopté à l’unanimité. La commune prévoit entre autres la construction d’une auberge clôturée de 12 chambres à Séguénéga, 4 boutiques à Gambo, 12 boutiques au marché de Séguénéga, un forage à Namassa, des toilettes au marché de Séguénéga, et un centre culturel et de loisirs avec 3 bureaux pour le Bureau communal de la jeunesse. Au titre des divers, les membres du conseil ont pris connaissance de la convention entre l’Agence d’Information du Burkina (AIB) et quitus a été donné à l'ordonnateur pour la concrétisation de ce partenariat qui permettrait la visibilité des activités majeures de la commune. La question de la climatisation de la morgue du CMA de Séguénéga, en panne depuis un certain temps, a également été évoquée. A la clôture de la session, Yacouba Guiro a rendu un vibrant hommage aux FDS et VDP qui sont sur le théâtre des opérations. L'autorité communale a sollicité l’accompagnement et l'engagement de tous les 20 membres de la délégation spéciale pour le développement de la commune. Agence d’Information du Burkina LG/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: Tone : Le Conseil régional offre des vivres et non-vivres à l’hôpital « Yendoubé » de Dapaong
items.description: Dapaong, 9 sept. (ATOP) – La pédiatrie et le centre de santé mentale de l’hôpital « Yendoubé » de Dapaong ont bénéficié, le mardi 8 septembre, d’un don de vivres et de non-vivres. Offert par le Conseil régional des Savanes, ce don est composé, entre autres, de sacs de riz, de détergents, de savons, de nattes et de lait pour bébé. Il vise à soutenir l’hôpital dans la prise en charge des patients qui ont des difficultés à se nourrir. Photo de famille devant le don Le président du Conseil régional des Savanes, Banlépo Nabaguédjoa, a fait savoir que ce geste constitue une marque de solidarité, de fraternité et de considération à l’endroit des personnes vulnérables. « Nous savons que les difficultés auxquelles vous êtes confrontés ne peuvent être résolues par une seule action. Toutefois, chaque aide compte, chaque contribution, aussi modeste soit-elle, peut apporter un soulagement», a-t-il indiqué. Le directeur régional de la Santé des Savanes, Dr Atcha Oubou Tinah, a exprimé sa gratitude au Conseil régional pour ce geste qui démontre l’importance accordée aux enfants et aux personnes confrontées à des problèmes de santé mentale. « Quand vous regardez ces catégories de personnes, ce sont des personnes vraiment vulnérables. Quand vous prenez les statistiques sanitaires en matière de mortalité et de morbidité, les enfants sont les plus touchés. Ainsi, lorsque nous recevons des dons, que ce soit des vivres ou des non-vivres, cela veut dire que c’est une vie sauvée », a-t-il déclaré. Les directrices de la pédiatrie et du centre de santé mentale de l’hôpital, respectivement, les Sœurs Catherine Marie Dayo et Espérance Sona, ont promis d’en faire un bon usage au bénéfice des personnes les plus nécessiteuses. Les deux responsables ont également souhaité que d’autres bonnes volontés emboîtent le pas au Conseil régional des Savanes afin de contribuer à une meilleure prise en charge des personnes vulnérables. ATOP/JK/MD

items.title: Nigeria High Commission cuts UK passport intervention fee to £20
items.description: Reduction follows backlash over £70 administrative charge LONDON — The Nigerian High Commission in the United Kingdom has reduced its fee for the ongoing passport intervention exercise from £70 to £20, following protests and scrutiny over the additional charge. The fee was reduced on Wednesday, although applicants were reportedly not formally notified of the change displayed on the commission’s website. TheCable had reported that the High Commission imposed an additional £70 administrative charge on applicants during the intervention exercise, despite an earlier directive issued under the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari limiting charges by Nigerian diplomatic missions for making their premises available for such exercises to £20. According to the report, the £70 administrative fee was imposed without approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while applicants were also charged £150 for lost passports. The intervention attracted Nigerians in the UK seeking urgent passport renewals, with applicants booking appointments through the High Commission’s online portal. TheCable reported that officials familiar with the exercise said fees were collected from about 3,000 applicants, despite the facility having the capacity to accommodate fewer than 300 people daily. Although the fee has now been reduced to £20, the newspaper reported that the charge still conflicts with the separate £20 administrative fee stipulated under the earlier directive. Officials involved in the exercise were quoted as saying that the High Commission had requested an additional payment to facilitate the process and generate revenue. Reacting to concerns over the exercise, Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said he was concerned about the inconvenience experienced by Nigerians seeking to renew their passports. Tunji-Ojo also denied knowledge of any approved administrative fee of the nature allegedly demanded by officials, saying consultations were ongoing with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to address the difficulties. On Tuesday, the Nigerian High Commission in London announced the suspension of biometric capturing for the passport intervention exercise in the city. Applicants were subsequently directed to alternative centres to continue with their appointments. items.title: Le conflit entre les Houthis et Riyad est à son plus haut niveau de tensions depuis 2022
items.description: Les Houthis ont mené hier, mardi 8 septembre, leurs frappes les plus importantes depuis le cessez-le-feu de 2022 négocié par l'ONU : quatre villes du sud de l'Arabie saoudite – Abha, Najran, Jizan et Khamis Mushait – ont été visées par plusieurs dizaines de drones et missiles balistiques, touchant notamment des installations d'Aramco ainsi que la base aérienne du roi Khalid. Ces frappes ont fait au moins 73 blessés civils et contraint plusieurs sites énergétiques à suspendre leur activité. Les Houthis ont présenté ces frappes comme une réponse à une attaque aérienne saoudienne survenue la veille, lundi 7 septembre, contre la prison d'Al-Hazm, dans le gouvernorat d'Al-Jawf, qui aurait fait 23 morts. Les tensions entre les deux camps avaient connu un nouveau pic en juillet, après l'attaque contre l'aéroport international de Sanaa, attribuée à l'Arabie saoudite par les Houthis, qui l'avaient qualifiée « d’agression flagrante ». Le gouvernement yéménite, soutenu par Riyad, avait revendiqué les frappes, accusant les Houthis d’avoir « violé la souveraineté yéménite » en autorisant un avion iranien à atterrir. Les frappes houthistes visent à porter atteinte à l'économie saoudienne afin de contraindre Riyad à mettre fin à sa campagne militaire au Yémen. Mardi 8 septembre, les médias officiels houthis ont indiqué que le groupe poursuivrait ses frappes sur les « artères économiques » saoudiennes tant que le royaume n'aurait pas cessé ses opérations militaires, levé son blocus sur les ports et aéroports sous contrôle houthi, versé les salaires de ses fonctionnaires et payé des réparations de guerre معادلات الردع اليمنية تُسقط أوهام العدو السعودي وتصيبه في مقتل », Saba , 8 septembre 2026.'> 1 . Le baril de Brent a dépassé les 100 dollars mercredi 9, pour la première fois depuis juillet. Riyad s'est engagé à riposter, tandis que le ministre pakistanais de la Défense a déclaré que l'Arabie saoudite pourrait activer la clause de défense mutuelle de l'accord de défense conjoint signé en août, et qui inclut aussi la Turquie Pakistan Pledges to Honor Security Pact If Saudi Arabia Attacked », Bloomberg , 9 septembre 2026.'> 2 . Une escalade du conflit pourrait compliquer les efforts américains visant à désamorcer la guerre avec l’Iran, à quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat. La Maison-Blanche a largement fait abstraction des frappes houthistes en mer Rouge visant des pétroliers saoudiens. Le groupe avait annoncé fin juillet un embargo sur les ports et les navires saoudiens, contraignant Riyad à trouver de nouvelles solutions de contournement pour ses exportations de pétrole, déjà perturbées par le blocus du détroit d’Ormuz. Les clients asiatiques d'Aramco sont les plus touchés par cette réorganisation logistique : les cargaisons chargées à Yanbu, sur la mer Rouge, transitent désormais par le canal de Suez pour éviter le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, avant de contourner l'Afrique pour rejoindre l'Asie – ce qui double la distance du trajet. Les frappes sur les infrastructures énergétiques saoudiennes pourraient marquer un tournant dans la stratégie houthiste, qui s’est jusqu’à présent principalement concentrée sur le trafic de pétrole en mer Rouge. Au moins huit pétroliers saoudiens ont été pris pour cible par les Houthis depuis l’annonce de l’embargo, le 20 juillet. L’article Le conflit entre les Houthis et Riyad est à son plus haut niveau de tensions depuis 2022 est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: PML-N, ANP senators spar over death of Gujranwala sanitary worker at Senate committee meeting
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A meeting of the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights turned acrimonious on Wednesday as PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali and ANP chief Senator Aimal Wali Khan clashed over the questioning of Suthra Punjab officials in connection with the death of a Gujranwala waste management worker. Chaired by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, the committee was reviewing the death of an employee of the Gujranwala Waste Management Company (GWMC), who allegedly died by suicide after receiving half his salary and facing termination of his contract. Tensions rose when Senator Khan pressed officials with pointed questions. Senator Ali interrupted, objecting to the tone. “Listen to them — you are conducting an inquiry and asking questions as if you are sitting in a police station,” he said. When a member suggested that the cameras be switched off, Ali said he had “nothing wrong to say”. “Speak properly,” he told Khan. “I am speaking properly — you speak properly too,” Khan shot back. Senators, including Qurratulain Marri, intervened to defuse the situation. Officials told the committee that the worker had been with GWMC from 2024 to 2025 and that his contract had expired on May 31. The alleged suicide, they said, occurred after his employment had ended. Khan alleged that the worker had been paid only half his salary. “A common labourer was pushed to the point where he took his own life,” he said. The GWMC CEO disputed this, saying bank records showed full salary payments and that the worker had performance issues. Committee members questioned why Suthra Punjab was engaging a third party for cleaning staff instead of recruiting workers directly. Senator Marri pointed out that the Suthra Punjab Act came into force in 2026, while the incident took place in 2025. “How was recruitment done before the institution formally existed?” she asked. Khan echoed the concern. The CEO said the sanitary worker had initially been engaged in 2025 through a contractor and was later rehired and deputed to the IT room of the Suthra Punjab office as a naib qasid. He was later dismissed on grounds of misconduct, the committee was told. The GWMC CEO said compensation had been provided to the worker’s widow and children, including a plot purchased with the help of a chamber of commerce. When Senator Khan asked why a plot had been given if the worker was not in service, he remarked: “If you give me a plot too, I will also be happy.” Officials suggested the worker may have had personal problems. The ANP chief rejected the claim, saying: “You casually made an allegation that there was a love affair involved in why he died.” The committee directed Suthra Punjab to submit all relevant documents and copies of the laws for 2025 and 2026 and asked whether any redressal mechanism existed beyond financial compensation. The chairperson directed that the deceased’s family be invited to the next meeting to present their position. On July 1, a Suthra Punjab worker set himself on fire in Gujranwala in protest against non-payment of his full salary. He succumbed to his injuries two days later. A CCTV camera recorded footage of the employee when he was coming out of the office where he had gone to complain against the contractor, later showing him dowsing himself in petrol in the corridor in the presence of some staff members. Some other employees present there rushed to save their colleague and threw water on him, the CCTV footage showed. An official said the contractor had been illegally deducting a major chunk of the workers’ Rs21,000 monthly salary. On July 17, the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights expressed concern over the worker’s alleged suicide. It sought complete records, including contracts, salary registers, tax documents and banking transactions, to examine possible violations. It also directed authorities to provide details of compensation and insurance for the deceased worker’s family. Other cases taken up The Additional IG Sindh briefed the committee on the case of Mir Raza. His father had reported him missing in July 2026. The first post-mortem was conducted on July 30, and a second was conducted at the request of the accused’s family. Senator Ali questioned the need for a second autopsy. The committee was told that the SHO had failed to preserve the crime scene and had shifted the body to the hospital. Both the SHO and DSP were suspended for negligence. The committee recommended the arrest of the SHO. On the Jaranwala incident of August 16, 2023, officials said 389 people had been arrested and several cases were under trial or had been concluded. Expressing concern over delays, the chairperson said the matter involved a minority community and required urgent resolution. Senator Ali stressed the need for justice and adequate compensation. The Chief Secretary’s representative said an assessment committee would evaluate losses with community representatives and that Rs2 million would be given to each affected family. The families, however, said the amount did not match their actual losses. The chairperson directed that compensation be determined on the basis of actual damages. The committee also reviewed the target killing of Ahmed Javed. It was told that the main accused, who was out on bail, was appearing in court with 40-50 people, allegedly intimidating witnesses. The committee recommended applying to the court to stop the practice. Senator Khan criticised the working of the CCD in Punjab and CTD in KP. The chairperson also questioned the NCCIA’s performance regarding alleged malicious social media material uploaded by the accused.

items.title: Pakistan among Arab and Muslim nations welcoming British ban on goods from Israeli settlers
items.description: Pakistan, along with seven other Arab and Muslim nations, on Wednesday welcomed the United Kingdom’s decision to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. UK imposed the trade measures on Tuesday, alongside Canada and France. The decision was announced by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to what he called “ethnic cleansing” by settlers in the West Bank. The joint statement by the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Turkiye, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates was published by the Foreign Office (FO) and expressed hope that the international community would take similar actions in line with international law, “holding accountable settlement organisations and individuals engaged in illegal settlement activities”. The ministers also welcomed the earlier joint statement on the Two-State Solution issued by the foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom. “They encourage the international community to build on these steps and adopt concrete measures to bring an end to activities that support or sustain illegal Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory,” the FO stated. It added that the seven nations consider the ban in line with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions, including Security Council resolution 2334 (2016). They also considered the decision in line with the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice of July 19, 2024, which obligated states “not to recognise as legal the situation arising from Israel’s unlawful occupation and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining the situation created by Israel’s occupation”. “In this regard, they reiterate their call for Israel to rescind all measures taken in connection with settlement activities and other measures aimed at altering the geographic and demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory,” the joint statement read. It additionally stressed that Gaza is an integral part of Palestine and called for the “full and immediate” implementation of US President Donald Trump’s Comprehensive ‘Plan to End the Gaza Conflict’. The ministers reiterated that the only viable path to achieving lasting and comprehensive peace was implementing the Two-State solution and creating an independent, sovereign, contiguous and viable Palestinian State, based on the June 4, 1967 borders and with Jerusalem as its capital, as per international law. Earlier today, Pakistan welcomed the United Kingdom-led decision to impose trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, saying that the illegal settlements undermined efforts towards a two-state solution, a separate statement from the FO read. Meanwhile, a joint statement by the foreign ministers of 12 nations, including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden, also expressed an intention to follow suit and stressed that the Israeli government’s actions in the West Bank undermined the possibility of a two-state solution. In a statement on its X account, the FO welcomed the decision and said: “The continued expansion of illegal settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory constitutes a blatant violation of international law as well as relevant UN Security Council resolutions.” Maintaining that Israel’s actions were a hindrance to a two-state solution, the FO also welcomed the joint statement by the 12 countries, which it said were considering “similar measures and support[ing] such efforts against the illegal Israeli settlements”. “Pakistan hopes that these measures will send a clear and unequivocal message of rejection of illegal actions in the occupied Palestinian territory,” the statement said. Islamabad reiterated support for Palestine, vowing to stand by its people and “their just struggle for self-determination”. In response to the UK’s actions, Israel ordered the closure of the UK’s consulate in Jerusalem earlier today. It also said it would expel British representatives at a centre monitoring the US-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza, bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces and ban 12 Britons, mostly members of parliament, from visiting the country. Miliband, in response, condemned Israel’s actions as “regrettable and damaging”. Speaking to BBC Radio , he also rejected suggestions that the sanctions would impact intelligence cooperation with Israel. “We have important intelligence and security relationships with Israel, and I’m confident they will continue,” he said, declining to go into details. “And I was very clear yesterday that we do believe in working with our Israeli partners when it comes to the threats they face from Iran,” he added.

Teacher retraining needed to tackle social media jargon in WASSCE – Adutwum
items.description: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for increased teacher professional development following concerns over the use of social media language and jargon in the 2026 West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE). According to him, the appearance of informal social media expressions in students’ examination scripts points to a growing difficulty among some students in distinguishing between language used on social media and the formal language expected in academic settings. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, September 9, Dr Adutwum said the development should not be viewed as a crisis but rather as an opportunity to strengthen teacher training and academic counselling in schools. “I don’t think the sky is falling. It’s not the end of the world, but it’s an opportunity for teacher retraining, professional development,” he said. Dr Adutwum stressed the need for teachers to identify and address such challenges within the classroom before students sit for external examinations. He said teachers should be equipped through continuous professional development and professional learning communities where emerging challenges affecting students’ academic performance can be discussed. “These issues can be discussed there, for teachers to then go back to their classrooms and be able to spot these things and advise students,” he explained. According to him, teachers should be able to caution students when they use inappropriate expressions in academic work and explain the possible consequences. He further argued that such issues should ideally be detected during classroom assessments and internal examinations rather than first becoming apparent in WASSCE scripts. Dr Adutwum also called for stronger academic counselling and guidance for students to help them understand the distinction between informal communication and the language required in formal examinations. He believes a combination of teacher retraining, classroom monitoring and student guidance can help address the challenge and ensure that social media jargon does not undermine students’ performance in future external examinations.

Free SHS Secretariat official denies bribery allegations at Kumasi CSSPS Resolution centre
items.description: The Deputy Ashanti Regional Coordinator of the Free Senior High School Secretariat, Michael Owusu Baafi, has rejected allegations of bribery at the Placement Resolution Centre at the Kumasi Technical Institute (KTI), assuring parents and students that no fee is required to resolve CSSPS placement concerns. Mr Baafi has urged parents and candidates not to hand money to individuals who claim they can influence school placements or intervene in challenges involving the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS). His caution comes amid allegations that some people at the centre have been demanding payments from parents before helping them with their placement difficulties. Mr Baafi maintained that the placement resolution exercise is completely free and that officials at the centre do not charge parents for their services. He explained that although candidates may need to print placement forms and other documents from facilities outside the centre, those services are optional and are not part of any official fee for resolving placement issues. He said he had personally warned parents against dealing with people who request money in exchange for assistance and had taken action against some individuals found engaging in such practices by removing them from the centre. Mr Baafi further cautioned that anyone who chooses to pay such individuals does so at their own risk, emphasising that the Ghana Education Service (GES) does not charge for school placement. He also disclosed that officials at the centre have been making additional efforts to help students beyond their routine responsibilities. According to him, some officials have been using their own resources and available data to contact schools directly in search of placements for students whose cases require further intervention. He added that officials have, in some instances, personally funded the printing and forwarding of placement documents to schools to facilitate direct admissions, without demanding payment from the affected families. “We don’t take money here. If you give any money to anybody, it’s at your own peril. We are admitting students for free,” Mr Baafi said.

items.title: Obi blockage: Call overzealous governors to order, Ejiofor tells Tinubu
items.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — A political analyst, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has called on President Bola Tinubu to rein in what he described as “overzealous” political actors, warning that unchecked political tension could consume the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. Ejiofor made the call in a statement on Wednesday titled, “Benue and the Dangerous Road to 2027: Political Intolerance Must Not Become the New Normal and Beyond Peter Obi, What the Benue Incident Means for Nigeria’s Democracy.” He cautioned that the road to the 2027 elections should be defined by ideas, tolerance and democratic competition rather than thuggery, obstruction and violence. Ejiofor said his intervention was not partisan but motivated by the need to protect the country’s democratic process. “I am not ordinarily accustomed to dabbling into partisan political activities, particularly as they relate to the affairs of political parties. However, when a dangerous aberration is allowed to persist unchecked, it risks becoming a convention; and when a convention is repeatedly tolerated, it may ultimately acquire the unfortunate character of a political culture,” he said. He noted that with political activities for the 2027 elections underway, presidential candidates and other political contestants were entitled, within the law, to move across the country, present their manifestoes and seek the support of Nigerians. He expressed concern over what he described as the emergence of political intolerance, intimidation and organised thuggery at the early stage of the electioneering season. Ejiofor particularly condemned the reported obstruction of Peter Obi and members of his entourage in Benue State while they were travelling to Yelwata, describing the incident as “profoundly disturbing.” He alleged that armed political thugs obstructed the convoy in the presence of security personnel, creating an atmosphere of intimidation. That Obi eventually left the scene unharmed, he said, should not diminish the seriousness of the incident. “The larger and far more dangerous question is: what message does such an incident send to other political actors, and ultimately to the Nigerian electorate?” he asked. According to him, allowing political actors to restrict the movement of opponents through force or intimidation could pave the way for political anarchy. “If a presidential candidate can be obstructed by political thugs from entering a state during the lawful discharge of his political activities, what happens when the campaign becomes more intense? “What happens when political rhetoric hardens, tempers rise and rival camps become more desperate? Democracy cannot survive where political disagreements are settled by the roadblock, the cudgel or the gun,” he said. Ejiofor also cautioned Governor Hyacinth Alia and other political office holders against allowing political supporters to abuse their positions or resort to intimidation. “Governor Hyacinth Alia and every other political office holder must understand that occupying a public office is not a licence to convert the state into a political fiefdom. The authority of a governor is constitutional; the authority of a political thug is neither constitutional nor democratic,” he said. He warned that Nigeria’s history of political violence showed that seemingly isolated incidents of intimidation could escalate into wider confrontation. Ejiofor further argued that political actors who engage in such conduct in the name of President Tinubu or the All Progressives Congress, APC, could ultimately damage the image of the administration. “Some of these overzealous actors may genuinely be labouring under the mistaken impression that they are helping President Bola Ahmed Tinubu or strengthening the ruling All Progressives Congress. Nothing could be farther from the truth. They are not helping the President; they are demarketing him,” he said. He urged the President to call political actors, particularly those holding constitutional offices, to order and ensure that political competition remained within democratic boundaries. “I therefore respectfully urge President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to call such overzealous political actors, particularly those in positions of constitutional authority, to order. “The appropriate battlefield for political contests is the marketplace of ideas, not the streets; the manifesto, not the machete; the ballot box, not the political thug,” Ejiofor said. He also urged governors and other political leaders to campaign on their records, policies, programmes and achievements, while allowing voters to freely assess and judge them at the polls. “With campaign activities now officially underway, there is an urgent need for civility, restraint, tolerance and strict adherence to democratic norms,” he added. The post Obi blockage: Call overzealous governors to order, Ejiofor tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kéran : Le Centre culturel ouvre ses portes au public
items.description: Kantè, 9 sept. (ATOP) – La cérémonie d’inauguration du Centre culturel de la commune Kéran 3 s’est déroulée à Nadoba, situé à 24 km à l’est de Kantè. La structure est érigée sur une superficie de 1,500 ha. Elle est dotée d’une capacité d’accueil de 300 places, d’un podium, d’un local servant de bureau au gérant, d’un local technique pour la sonorisation et les projections vidéo et d’un bloc de sanitaire. L’édifice est également équipé d’un forage photovoltaïque d’une capacité de 5 m³ couplé d’extension d’eau dans l’enceinte de la structure. Ce centre culturel permettra d’accueillir diverses manifestations socioculturelles dans la dynamique de la valorisation du patrimoine local. Vue partielle de la façade principale du Centre culturel Le responsable des Appuis aux collectivités locales à la Société autonome de financement à l’entretien routier, Tchakoutè Kpètre a précisé que cette réalisation s’inscrit dans le volet sociétal de la SAFER au profit des communautés, bénéficiaires du patrimoine culturel «Otammari». Au nom de la population bénéficiaire, le maire de la commune Kéran 3, Fakounafah Batinata a relevé l’aspect éducatif, culturel et social de ce cadre idéal et convivial pour des réunions et des prestations culturelles au profit des populations locales. Il s’est engagé à une gestion efficace et efficiente de ce joyau pour le rayonnement de la commune Kéran 3. Sur financement de la SAFER, les travaux ont été exécutés par les entreprises Construire pour l’humain (CON.HU Sarl-U) et Delta Négoces Forages (DN-FOR) sous le contrôle de la Centrale des études et de construction (CEC). L’évènement a été marqué par la coupure symbolique du ruban et la remise des clés aux autorités communales en présence du secrétaire général de la préfecture, Bello Séfiou, des députés et cadres ainsi que d’autres autorités administratives et traditionnelles. La cérémonie a pris fin avec une visite guidée des locaux et la mise en terre de plants. ATOP/PAP/SED

items.title: Kankan : la mairie durcit les règles sur l’hébergement des étrangers et l’insalubrité
items.description: La mairie de Kankan annonce de nouvelles mesures visant à renforcer le contrôle des personnes accueillies dans les familles et à lutter contre l’insalubrité dans la commune urbaine. Dans un communiqué signé le 7 septembre 2026 par le maire Lamine Labo Kourouma, les autorités communales mettent notamment l’accent sur l’hébergement des personnes venues d’autres localités et la gestion des eaux usées. Désormais, « tout chef de famille qui reçoit un étranger venant d’une autre localité est tenu d’informer immédiatement le chef de quartier », précise le communiqué. La mairie va plus loin et indique qu’« il est formellement interdit à tout citoyen de loger un étranger sans en informer au préalable le chef de quartier ». Sur le volet assainissement, les autorités communales annoncent également des mesures contre les personnes qui déversent les eaux usées dans les caniveaux. « Les citoyens qui canalisent les eaux usées et de toilettes dans les caniveaux seront interpellés et sanctionnés par les chefs de quartier », prévient la mairie. Les fosses septiques à ciel ouvert sont également dans le viseur des autorités. Selon le communiqué, « ceux qui creusent des fosses septiques à ciel ouvert, même sur un chantier non achevé, seront également interpellés par le chef de quartier ». Autre mesure annoncée : les personnes installées devant le marché de Kankancoura et qui en masquent la devanture sont sommées de quitter les lieux. « Vous êtes sommées de quitter la devanture et de regagner l’intérieur du marché », indique la mairie, qui invite les personnes concernées à se rapprocher d’Ousmane Diallo, administrateur du marché de Kankancoura, pour toute information. En conclusion, la mairie de Kankan appelle les citoyens au civisme et au respect de ces nouvelles dispositions, qu’elle présente comme nécessaires « dans l’intérêt de la sécurité, de la salubrité et du bon fonctionnement de notre commune ». items.title: Poutine reçoit le président vietnamien au Kremlin et met en avant le renforcement de la coopération économique, énergétique et stratégique entre les deux pays
items.description: Les presidents russe et vietnamien se sont retrouves ce 9 septembre au Kremlin pour des negociations centrees sur l'avenir des relations bilaterales. Vladimir Poutine et To Lam ont d'abord participe a une ceremonie officielle au Grand Palais du Kremlin, avant l'ouverture des discussions entre les deux delegations. To Lam se trouve en Russie depuis le 7 septembre dans le cadre d'une visite d'etat. Le dirigeant vietnamien, qui cumule les fonctions de president du pays et de secretaire general du Parti communiste, avait rencontre la veille le Premier ministre russe Mikhaïl Michoustine. Les echanges au Kremlin ont porte sur le developpement du partenariat strategique global entre la Russie et le Vietnam. Commerce, cooperation scientifique et educative, echanges humanitaires, securite et defense figurent parmi les principaux dossiers. Les deux dirigeants devaient egalement aborder plusieurs questions internationales et regionales, ainsi que l'adoption de nouveaux documents bilateraux. a l'ouverture des negociations, Vladimir Poutine a insiste sur la diversite de cette cooperation. « Nous continuons a travailler dans tous les autres domaines. Cela concerne la culture, l'education et les questions de securite », a declare le president russe, evoquant egalement des projets qui ont deja fait leurs preuves et de « nouvelles initiatives interessantes ». To Lam maintient la ligne de Hanoï envers la Russie La rencontre a egalement ete marquee par une declaration politique de To Lam sur les relations avec Moscou. « Certains pays ont recemment exprime leur reaction au maintien par le Vietnam de bonnes relations avec la Russie. Cependant, le Vietnam n'a pas hesite et n'a pas change de position », a-t-il declare. Le president vietnamien n'a pas precise quels etats etaient concernes. Sa declaration reaffirme neanmoins la ligne suivie par Hanoï dans ses relations avec Moscou et sa volonte de poursuivre leur developpement. To Lam a par ailleurs remercie Vladimir Poutine et le peuple russe pour leur accueil, ainsi que pour les felicitations adressees a l'occasion du 81e anniversaire de l'independance du Vietnam. Commerce et energie au cœur de la cooperation Les relations entre les deux pays s'appuient aussi sur des echanges economiques en progression. Vladimir Poutine a rappele que le commerce bilateral avait augmente de pres de 6 % en 2025, depassant alors les 6 milliards de dollars. Au premier semestre 2026, le rythme de croissance des echanges a pratiquement double, selon le president russe. L'energie demeure l'un des secteurs les plus anciens de cette cooperation. La Russie et le Vietnam travaillent ensemble depuis plusieurs decennies dans le petrole et le gaz, notamment a travers plusieurs coentreprises. Historiquement centree sur les hydrocarbures, cette cooperation energetique s'elargit aujourd'hui au nucleaire civil. Rosatom a ainsi lance en juillet la construction d'un centre de sciences et de technologies nucleaires au Vietnam. Le groupe russe participe egalement au projet de centrale de Ninh Thuan-1, qui doit etre equipee de deux reacteurs VVER-1200. etablies en 1950, les relations diplomatiques entre Moscou et Hanoï se sont progressivement renforcees. Les deux pays ont conclu un partenariat strategique en 2001, eleve au rang de partenariat strategique global en 2012. La rencontre du Kremlin vient ainsi prolonger une relation ancienne que Moscou et Hanoï cherchent a developper davantage dans les domaines economique, energetique, securitaire, educatif et politique.

items.title: L’Assemblée nationale et ONU-Habitat s’accordent pour sauver les villes camerounaises
items.description: © AN Au lendemain du lancement du Plan national villes intelligentes, le partenariat se renforce au sommet. Ce 9 septembre 2026, le président de l'Assemblée nationale, Théodore Datouo, a reçu à Yaoundé Mme Anacláudia Rossbach, sous-secrétaire générale des Nations Unies et directrice exécutive d'ONU-Habitat. Une audience qui s'est tenue en présence de la ministre de l'Habitat et du Développement urbain, Célestine Ketcha Courtès. Si l'ensemble du Cameroun est concerné, c'est la capitale qui a cristallisé les échanges. La patronne d'ONU-Habitat a pointé du doigt les conséquences directes de l'étalement urbain anarchique de Yaoundé sur l'environnement, le climat, les populations et l'activité économique. Elle a abouti au diagnostic selon lequel sans une meilleure planification foncière et territoriale, la ville va continuer à s'étendre au détriment de tout. Elle a plaidé pour une urbanisation maîtrisée et inclusive. Pour accompagner la dynamique, ONU-Habitat a mis sur la table trois leviers. Il s’agit de la décentralisation pour donner plus de pouvoir aux mairies ; de la localisation des ODD pour adapter les objectifs du développement durable aux réalités de chaque ville ; la promotion et la valorisation des matériaux locaux pour construire. Elle a surtout insisté sur un point : il faut une collaboration étroite entre le parlement et le gouvernement pour créer des lois adaptées. De son côté, le président de l'Assemblée nationale a assuré que le Cameroun a "des bases solides" pour renforcer ce partenariat avec l'ONU. Il a mis en avant deux priorités pour le parlement : faciliter l'accès des femmes au logement et à la propriété foncière, présenté comme un levier essentiel d'autonomisation ; accompagner par des lois les efforts pour une urbanisation mieux planifiée. Après l'Exécutif hier avec le lancement du Plan villes intelligentes, c'est désormais le Législatif qui s'engage à créer le cadre juridique pour que ce plan ne reste pas lettre morte. Cet article L’Assemblée nationale et ONU-Habitat s'accordent pour sauver les villes camerounaises est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Obi attacks signal possible violence in 2027 polls — ASITU
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Association of Igbo Town Unions, ASITU, has condemned the reported attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Coalition, NDC, Peter Obi, in Benue State, warning that such incidents could signal the possibility of violence during the 2027 general elections. Obi’s convoy was reportedly attacked by a group of youths on the Makurdi-Gboko road while he was travelling to Yelwata to sympathise with victims of recent attacks in the community. ASITU also alleged that Obi had previously come under attack during a visit to Benin City, Edo State. The association warned that repeated attacks on political candidates could create a dangerous atmosphere ahead of the 2027 elections and urged authorities to act swiftly to prevent further incidents. National President of ASITU, Chief Emeka Diwe, stated this in an interview with Vanguard, expressing concern over the reported Benue incident, particularly because Obi was in the state to visit victims of the attacks in Yelwata. The group called on the Federal and Benue State governments to investigate the incident and ensure that those found responsible were brought to justice. ASITU said: “The attacks on the presidential candidate of the NDC, Mr Peter Obi, have become too many. He was attacked in Benin City and now in Benue State. “The attack in Benue State is shocking because Obi was only in the state to sympathise with victims of terror attacks in Yelwata. “We warn that these attacks are looming signals that the 2027 general elections may be marred by violence. Nigerians should be free to campaign in any part of the country. “Some state governors have threatened Obi against visiting their states, yet the security agencies have done nothing over the threats. The Benue State government should ensure that this incident is investigated.” The association also called on the Federal Government to step up efforts to identify and prosecute those allegedly sponsoring attacks on political figures. “Today, it is Mr Peter Obi; tomorrow, it may be another candidate or a high-ranking Nigerian. These are also signs that no part of the country is safe as we get to the 2027 elections. “The Tinubu administration must do something about these attacks before it is too late,” the group said.
